denominator.definition: Total number of census tracts designated as Qualified Opportunity Zones in the initial 2018 designation round (first and final rounds combined)
denominator.value: 8,761 communities in 50 states, DC, and 5 U.S. territories

candidates.statement: Opportunity Zone designation authority granted by the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017, codified in section 1400Z-2 of the Internal Revenue Code.
Designation process: State governors and chief executive officers nominate eligible low-income census tracts; U.S. Treasury Department certifies and designates the nominated zones.
First round designations announced April 9, 2018, covering 18 states. Final round announced June 14, 2018, completing designation in all 50 states plus DC and 5 territories.
Eligible tracts defined as: (1) low-income communities meeting IRS definition, or (2) non-LIC contiguous tracts nominated alongside LIC tracts, limited to 25% of state's eligible LIC tracts.
GAO found selected tracts had higher poverty and greater share of non-White populations than eligible but unselected tracts; differences statistically significant.
GAO identified data collection gaps: no single agency designated to collect comprehensive performance data on Opportunity Zone investments and tax compliance.
As of 2019, more than 6,000 Qualified Opportunity Funds had invested approximately $29 billion, based on partial IRS data.
Tax incentive structure (section 1400Z-2): investors can defer gain recognition on amounts invested in QOFs within 180 days; gain exclusion applies for holding periods of 5, 7, or 10+ years.
